I will keep my land in the usual North China Plain rotation: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the system I trust most in Quzhou County because I know how to manage it, I already understand the field work rhythm, and it gives me the most stable grain output over the whole year. I will not spread myself across too many crops. I would rather stay with the crops I can manage well, use improved or hybrid seed, control fertilizer instead of pushing it too hard, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide use to the minimum I think is necessary for weeds, aphids, rust, and corn pests. For wheat, I will focus on strong seedlings, spring water and fertilizer timing, and disease control before heading. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize, keep the stubble, seed directly with little delay, feed it mainly around the jointing and big-bell stage, and watch closely for drought and insects. That is the plan I would follow this year because it balances yield, cost, labor, and risk.
